fatal_errors: Places the mechanism above 500 °C and potentially in chloride media, whereas the target tribo-corrosion tests were conducted in deionized water at 25–100 °C; the approximately 1100 °C exposure was only rapid thermal-shock conditioning.
Uses isolated wear and isolated corrosion as the principal baseline instead of identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205 and the within-alloy 25 °C reference.
Predicts generally accelerated, superadditive degradation without reconstructing the observed nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum loss near 50 °C and maximum loss at 100 °C.
Does not predict the HEA's substantially lower wear, friction, and electrochemical degradation relative to DS2205 or connect this performance to retention of the L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
explanation: The hypothesis captures one component of the target mechanism: repeated formation, fracture, and removal of an oxide or tribo-layer can expose fresh metal and couple wear to corrosion. This is most consistent with the target's 100 °C regime. However, it incorrectly recasts the experiment as high-temperature oxidation above 500 °C, misses the aqueous 25–100 °C conditions, and omits the transition from abrasion at 25 °C to stable-film polishing at 50 °C and disrupted oxidative or third-body wear at 100 °C. Its proposed three-arm wear-only/corrosion-only/combined experiment is capable of testing superadditive synergy and cyclic film removal, but it would not by itself distinguish the target explanation concerning temperature-dependent film stability or HEA-versus-DS2205 behavior. No supporting evidence is supplied, and several mechanistic claims—phase-selective oxidation, highly corrosion-susceptible exposed phases, and degradation exceeding the sum of isolated contributions—remain unsupported.
